sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].

The path was cyclical rather than smooth: a 22.4% drop in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198] was followed by a 22.1% rebound in FY2021 [F6][D251] and a 12.8% rise in FY2023 to $67.1 billion [F8][D357].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].

The FY2023 gain was primarily favorable price realization and higher sales volume [P32], while FY2025's 4.3% growth to $67.6 billion [F10][D463] came from higher sales volume partly offset by unfavorable price realization [P13].
Power & Energy is now the largest segment at 47.6% of revenue in FY2025 [D757], up from 41.8% in FY2023 [D753], and it added 5.2pp of the 4.3% revenue growth [D759][D463].
Power Generation alone grew 32.5% in FY2025 [D894], contributing 3.9pp [D895], while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D765][D766].
Construction Industries' decline was primarily unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume of $568 million [P8].
Operating income grew far faster than revenue over the window, at a 28.6% CAGR against 6.4% [F202][F201], but FY2025 reversed: operating income fell 14.7% [D464] on 4.3% revenue growth [D463].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% in FY2025 [D467], in line with the 17.7% net income decline [D465], as the 3.5% share-count reduction [D483] only partly cushioned the drop.
Operating margin was 16.5% in FY2025 [F30], above the 14.3% window median [D1123] but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [F29][D1122] and far above the 3.0% FY2016 low [F21][D1121].
The FY2025 margin fell 3.7pp [D476], with cost of revenue subtracting 4.2pp [D490] while SG&A and R&D were roughly neutral [D492][D491].

Operating profit fell $1.921 billion primarily on unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million, with manufacturing costs largely reflecting higher tariffs [P9].
Net margin of 13.1% [F50] sat 3.4pp below operating margin [F30], as a 24.0% effective tax rate [D449] and $892 million of other income [X110] partly offset the gap.
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion [F80] covered net income of $8.9 billion [F40], a 1.32x conversion [D450] against a 1.07x industrials peer median [D1154].
Free cash flow margin was 13.2% [D447], above the 11.9% median [D1129] but below the 16.8% FY2023 high [D1128], as capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion [F90][D470].
Capex reached 1.25x D&A in FY2025 [D452], the highest in the window, against 0.37x in FY2016 [D10].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion primarily on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].
Net debt widened to $26.2 billion in FY2025 [D456] from $24.9 billion in FY2024 [D403], as total debt grew 14.1% [D485] and cash rose 44.9% to $10.0 billion [F140][D484].
Net cash was -38.8% of revenue [D457], slightly worse than the -35.6% industrials peer median [D1152], at the 43rd percentile of seven peers [D1151].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion and dividends of $2.7 billion [X140][X150] consumed 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Return on average equity of 43.5% [D462] ranked at the 100th percentile of six peers against a 23.3% median [D1155][D1156].
Net debt has deepened for two straight years, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 [D350] to $24.9 billion [D403] and $26.2 billion [D456], as debt-funded buybacks outran free cash flow [R1].
Revenue fell 3.4% in FY2024 to $64.8 billion [F9][D410] on lower sales volume, partly offset by favorable price realization [P22][R2].
Net income for FY2021 through FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's rounded pay-versus-performance figures, differing from the 10-K by up to 0.06% [R3][X16][X20].
Segment revenue members on one axis sum to 219% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so segment lines should not be added together [R6].

Operating margin: a print below the 14.3% window median [D1123] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the tariff-driven compression seen in FY2025 [P9], while a return above 20.2% [D1122] would reverse it.
Free cash flow margin: holding above the 11.9% median [D1129] would show the capex step-up to 4.2% of revenue [D446] is digestible; a drop toward the 9.7% FY2018 low [D1127] would not.
Net cash: a further move below the FY2025 level of -$26.2 billion [D456] would extend the two-year deterioration [R1], while a narrowing toward the FY2023 -$22.1 billion [D350] would reverse it.
